concept.name: Normal day
concept.definition: A Market Profile day type in which the initial balance (first-hour range) is average to wide and holds for most of the session: the market rotates within or just beyond that early range, building a balanced, bell-shaped distribution with the point of control near the center. It is the most common day type, reflecting two-sided trade dominated by short-term participants.
concept.intuition: A normal day is the market's default setting: an early range is established, longer-term players see no reason to reprice, and the day rotates around fair value.
concept.mechanics: Identified by a wide initial balance that is not meaningfully extended (at most a minor one-sided extension), single-print tails at both extremes showing lack of other-timeframe conviction, and the close near the middle of the range.
concept.failure_modes: The label is retrospective; a 'normal day' in progress can be transformed by a late news-driven range extension, so plans built on balance must survive that failure.
concept.misconceptions: Normal days are not low-information days to ignore — their wide value areas become key references for subsequent sessions, and the classification says nothing about the next day's direction.
concept.example: The first hour spans 4,505–4,535; the rest of the session rotates inside that range, the POC builds at 4,520, and the market closes at 4,522 — a classic normal day.

citations.source: Marketcalls — Market Profile: Different Types of Profile Days (normal day)
